title: RK Royal Kludge R87 Pro Wired Mechanical Keyboard $66.18; RK M20 Wireless Numpad Keyboard $39.86 Delivered @ Royal Kludge
body:
Deal: RK Royal Kludge R87 Pro Wired Mechanical Keyboard $66.18; RK M20 Wireless Numpad Keyboard $39.86 Delivered @ Royal Kludge

[Recollect9764] Website sure is interesting, I almost immediately got a popup that prompted me to "Subsirbe our Newsletter and get 2% Discount"
[NEWLAND] Hi friend. It is our new event popup. It also includes reminders for our weekly lucky draw, which is to encourage everyone to participate in the event in a timely manner.
[I like GoodDeals] @NEWLAND, The point is subscribe spelling is listed as - 'Subsirbe' on your website.
[Fullhalter] Which RK tri-mode models support qmk/via? Preferably tkl and larger
[NEWLAND] Hi friend. Only our R75 Pro keyboard. Link here: https://www.ozbargain.com.au/node/969534
[dramant88] Any deals on wired 96-100%? Can't live without a numpad for desktop.
[NEWLAND] RK 96 here: https://www.ozbargain.com.au/node/968403
Next week I will update some other products with numpad, as these products will arrive at our Australian warehouse around the same time.
[dramant88] No worries, let me know if there are any 98-100%, don't think I could get used to the reduced space easily.
[chickentaste] I have a couple of RK keyboards, they're great. They hit the perfect sweet spot between value and quality. Typing this on an RK S104 right now!
[ShinyDiamond] Could someone please suggest a full size (100%), mechanical wireless keyboard, with firm tactile bounce and clicky sounds (like blue switches). But I need plug ang play out of the box without any software modifications (can't install any software on office computer). Need with a usb dongle.
Thanks in advance.
[Naigrabzo] Check out AJAZZ ones. They are quite good IMHO. I have one at home but in the office blue keys might piss off ya peers.
[Elision] Every time I see a deal for this site I can't help but wonder who the heck thought "Royal Kludge" was a nice name for an electronics brand…Kludge is a terrible sounding word hahaha. Especially when it means "to put something, especially computer hardware or software, together from whatever is available, especially when it does not work very well"
I will say in my head I was pronouncing it like it rhymed with Sludge, when it's pronounced like Klooj (if the name is meant to be somehow based on that specific word/pronounciation), slightly less terrible.
